project_name: AWS Richmond County Data Center Campus
aliases: Amazon Richmond County AI and Cloud Campus
Energy Way Industrial Park AWS campus
status_detail: Amazon announced a $10B data center/AI campus in Richmond County in June 2025; DCD reported groundbreaking in October 2025. Cleanview tracks multiple 65 MW Blue Marlin buildings planned from 2027 through later phases; campus-scale MW inferred from 20 x 65 MW tracked buildings and should be treated as tracker-derived.
notes: Largest confirmed NC data center investment found; WRAL says first building projected operational in 2027 with additional facilities through 2029.

status_detail: Tracked as a 225,000 sq ft planned building in Amazon's Richmond County campus, expected operational in 2027.
notes: Separate building retained because the brief requests wide project coverage and Cleanview exposes AWS phases as project rows.

status_detail: Tracked as part of Amazon's Richmond County phased campus; expected operational in 2027.
notes: Cleanview lists Building 2 among the largest planned NC data centers.

status_detail: Tracked as part of Amazon's Richmond County phased campus; expected operational in 2027.

project_name: Microsoft Catawba County Data Center Program
status_detail: Catawba County says Microsoft plans at least $1B for four data centers over 10 years; local reports describe construction impacts at Conover. DCMap tracks Lyle Creek as under construction with 448 MW.
notes: Official county statement names four data centers but does not provide MW; capacity is tracker-derived.

project_name: Microsoft Person County Mega Park Data Center Campus
aliases: Person County Mega Park Data Center
status_detail: Microsoft bought the Person County Mega Park and county/Microsoft communications say permitting for data center development is expected to begin in 2026; detailed plans not yet public.
notes: Early-stage campus on roughly 1,350-1,385 acres near Woodsdale/Roxboro.

status_detail: Google's official Lenoir timeline says the data center opened in 2008; Cleanview tracks Building 1 at 39 MW.
notes: Capacity is tracker-derived; official Google source confirms campus and opening year.

status_detail: Cleanview tracks Building 2 as operational in 2011 at 72 MW; Google official page confirms continuing Lenoir campus operations.
notes: Building-level capacity/year from tracker.

status_detail: Cleanview tracks Building 3 as operational in 2015 at 148 MW; Google official page confirms Lenoir campus milestones and ongoing operations.
notes: Building-level capacity/year from tracker.

status_detail: City of Lenoir reported Google's new two-year $1B North Carolina data center investment in 2026; Cleanview tracks Building 4 as planned for 2026 at 91 MW.
notes: Capacity and specific building label are tracker-derived.

aliases: Apple North Carolina data center campus
status_detail: Apple selected Maiden in 2009 and built a large campus; 2025 reporting says Apple is adding a $175M, 237,600 sq ft data center on land it already owns. DCMap tracks Maiden 2 at 223.5 MW operational.
notes: Includes operating campus plus current expansion signal; exact campus MW varies by tracker/building.

project_name: Meta Forest City Data Center Campus
status_detail: Rutherford County EDC announced Facebook/Meta expansion including a third data center; DCMap tracks the Forest City campus at 150 MW operational.
notes: Cleanview also splits the campus into buildings at 35 MW, 30 MW, and 40 MW; campus-level tracker capacity is higher.

status_detail: Core Scientific official campus page lists 117 MW total power capacity, 70 acres, and 250,000 sq ft at Marble, NC; WUNC reports conversion from crypto mining toward AI workloads.
notes: Core Scientific social material references about 65 MW billable AI-ready capacity upon completion; official page total power is used in capacity_mw.

project_name: WhiteFiber NC-1 Madison AI Data Center Campus
aliases: Bit Digital WhiteFiber Madison AI Campus
status_detail: WhiteFiber announced NC-1 with 24 MW operational power and 99 MW secured power; Nscale signed for 40 MW at the campus with capacity available in 2026.
notes: Some trackers list 200 MW longer-term scale potential; 99 MW secured power used as conservative structured capacity.

aliases: Town Lane and PowerHouse Charlotte campus
status_detail: PowerHouse/Town Lane acquired 122 acres for a five-building Charlotte campus with 300 MW secured power, expandable to 500 MW; AREP says grading is underway and first building is targeted for April 2027.
notes: Located around University City Boulevard; public materials vary between 1.5M and 2.5M sq ft.

status_detail: Digital Realty filed for a 156-acre, roughly 400 MW data center campus at 12899 Moores Chapel Road; local coverage says Charlotte City Council approved rezoning on May 19, 2026.
notes: Planned two-building, up to 3M sq ft telecommunications/data storage campus.

status_detail: Digital Realty lists Charlotte data centers in First Ward; DCMap tracks 731 E Trade St as an operational 12 MW Digital Realty facility.
notes: Existing metro colocation/interconnection facility, separate from the proposed Moores Chapel campus.

status_detail: Project website describes a proposed campus on about 190 acres with four 200,000 sq ft data center buildings near New Hill; trackers/news report local opposition, Apex/Chatham moratorium pressure, and some withdrawal signals, so status remains high-risk planned.
notes: Capacity from DCMap/Cleanview; official site gives buildings and location but not MW.

aliases: Triangle Innovation Point West Data Center
developer: Eco TIP West LLC / Lee-Moore Capital
status_detail: Eco TIP West sued Chatham County over a one-year data center moratorium; local reporting says the developer claims vested rights after spending over $11M on an approximately 750 MW data center at TIP West.
notes: CBRE markets TIP West as a 339-acre pre-graded data center site with Duke load studies completed; legal outcome may change status.

status_detail: Proposed 1,800-acre data center campus near Walnut Cove/Belews Creek; January 2026 rezoning approval was later voided after lawsuit and the developer planned to resubmit. Capacity often described as several hundred MW; some social/local references cite much larger figures but are less certain.
notes: Set capacity_mw to 300 as a conservative representation of 'several hundred megawatts'; exact size not officially pinned down.

aliases: Energy Storage Solutions Kingsboro AI data center
status_detail: Originally proposed as a $19.2B, 900 MW AI data center campus at Kingsboro Business Park; Triangle Business Journal and other 2026 sources report Energy Storage Solutions withdrew the proposal in July 2026.
notes: Retained because brief explicitly requests early announcements and no deletion; use status_detail rather than dropping withdrawn project.

project_name: Energy Storage Solutions Tarboro Data Center
status_detail: Separate earlier Energy Storage Solutions proposal in Tarboro was rejected by the Tarboro Town Council/Edgecombe officials after local opposition; DCK described it as a 100 MW project before the larger Kingsboro effort.
notes: Rejected/canceled proposal preserved as early-announcement evidence.

status_detail: DCMap tracks Fayetteville NetZero Campus as a planned 50 MW Energy Storage Solutions project in Fayetteville.
notes: Low-public-detail tracker entry; needs future permit/EDA confirmation.

status_detail: Tract proposed a 400-acre master-planned data center campus near Mooresville with up to five buildings and 1.5M sq ft; later tracker/local sources report the rezoning application was withdrawn in August 2025.
notes: Retained because it was publicly proposed even though withdrawn.

status_detail: Compass proposed a roughly 333-acre, five-building data center campus on Stamey Farm Road; City of Statesville FAQ says the Compass project is approved and exempt from a proposed moratorium. JLL/DCD reporting cites up to 500 MW.
notes: Cleanview gives expected operational year 2028; capacity from marketed power capacity/tracker.

status_detail: Trackers report 5C is developing a Charlotte AI data center campus launching with 50 MW critical IT capacity and designed to scale to 1,600 MW; Baxtel says planned for 2026 with expansions through 2028.
notes: High MW figure is tracker-derived; official 5C page confirms data center business but does not expose a Charlotte-specific public detail page in search results.

project_name: Raeden Gateway Research Park Data Center
status_detail: ImpactData and Raeden announced a 20 MW phase-one AI-capable colocation data center at Gateway Research Park with Q2 2026 target and 300 MW+ subsequent scale potential.
notes: Structured capacity records full scale potential; phase-one MW is 20.

status_detail: Local reporting and trackers describe DigiPower X's proposed 200 MW AI/data center on land it owns off Cline Park Court near a Duke substation; zoning updates were moving forward in March 2026.
notes: Baxtel lists planned 2028 with expansions through 2029; local opposition noted.

project_name: PointOne / CyrusOne Lee County Data Center
aliases: PointOne Lower Moncure Road data center
status_detail: PointOne submitted plans for a Lee County campus at 4079 Lower Moncure Road; reports and CyrusOne's site say CyrusOne will own/operate a multiphase campus near Sanford, with a 90 MW IT-load first phase and completion targeted for 2028.
notes: First-phase building described as about 300,000 sq ft on 56 acres within a larger 400-430 acre site.

status_detail: Cleveland County EDP and T5 materials describe the Kings Mountain data center campus with a 180 MW substation; DCMap tracks T5 Charlotte Campus as operational at 180 MW.
notes: Campus marketed as west of Charlotte with purpose-built powered shell.

project_name: DC BLOX High Point Data Center
status_detail: High Point EDC announced DC BLOX would build and operate a multi-tenant data center on a 14-acre tract at 4131 Sheraton Court; DCD reported up to 54,000 sq ft and 18 MW power capacity.
notes: Investment described as up to $305M including induced customer equipment.

status_detail: CyrusOne's official DUR1 page lists a Durham, NC carrier-neutral facility with 50 MW total IT capacity.
notes: Former Sentinel facility acquired by CyrusOne; included as a major operating NC project.

project_name: Data Journey Catawba County Data Center

status_detail: Data Journey acquired the former Bed Bath & Beyond Catawba County data center in 2024; DCD reported 47,500 sq ft with expansion beyond 3 MW critical load and longer-range power-generation exploration; DCMap tracks 30 MW.
notes: Capacity varies by source; DCMap's 30 MW used in structured field, DCD gives smaller current critical-load expansion.
